*F-IBE* (Identity-based encryption) is part of *Public-Key Primitives, Key Exchange, Messaging* in the UC functionality encyclopedia. Status: an emerging formulation, still an active area of research.

**This entry is blocked, and the block is worth stating precisely rather than leaving the page blank.** A canonical definition exists; it is located; it could not be read. So this page carries neither a box nor a *No canonical definition* claim — the latter would be false, and the field on this page is the one value `scripts/uc_status.py` will not derive precisely because it is an assertion about the literature.

## What exists, and where

Nishimaki, Manabe and Okamoto define the ideal functionality of identity-based encryption, $\mathcal{F}_{\mathsf{IBE}}$, and prove the result that makes it worth transcribing: **UC-secure IBE is equivalent to conventionally secure — IND-ID-CCA2-secure — IBE.** That is the same shape of theorem as the one behind [*F-PKE*](/uc/layer-3-public-key-primitives/f-pke/index.qmd)'s object, and it is the reason an IBE functionality is a definition rather than a restatement: it says the composable notion costs nothing over the game-based one, which is not true of [*F-ABE*](/uc/layer-3-public-key-primitives/f-abe/index.qmd) one step up the generality ladder, where standard ABE is *not* composably secure against an active adversary.

The work appears twice: at VIETCRYPT 2006 (LNCS 4341, pp. 337–353) and as a journal version in IEICE Transactions on Fundamentals E91-A(1), pp. 262–271, January 2008.

## Why it is not transcribed

**Neither version is obtainable.** It is not on the Cryptology ePrint Archive — searched by title, by author and by the equivalence result. The Springer chapter and the IEICE and J-STAGE journal pages are paywalled and return HTML rather than a PDF. The authors' own publication list names both versions and offers no full text for either.

The rule this site is held to is that you never cite a version you did not read, and never transcribe a definition you have not seen. A box written from the abstract and from secondary descriptions would be exactly the fabrication that rule exists to prevent — the most damaging thing an entry here can produce, because it is the least likely to be caught. So the entry stops.

## What would resolve this

1. **Obtain either version and transcribe it.** This is a five-minute job for anyone with institutional access to Springer or IEICE, and it is the entire remaining work on this page. That is worth saying plainly: this is not a research gap, it is a library-access gap.
2. **Find a later paper that reprints $\mathcal{F}_{\mathsf{IBE}}$.** Functionalities are often reproduced "for completeness" by papers that build on them, which is how [*F-CKE*](/uc/layer-3-public-key-primitives/f-cke/index.qmd)'s box would have been recoverable had its source been closed. No such reprint was found here, but the search was not exhaustive.

## What is nearby on this site

[*F-ABE*](/uc/layer-3-public-key-primitives/f-abe/index.qmd) is the generalization, and its page carries a printed box together with the impossibility that makes IBE's equivalence result notable by contrast. [*F-PKE*](/uc/layer-3-public-key-primitives/f-pke/index.qmd) and [*F-rPKE*](/uc/layer-3-public-key-primitives/f-rpke/index.qmd) are the ordinary public-key case. None of the three is a substitute for the box this page is missing, and none is blended in.
